item: Unlock: the page says what the passphrase check is recovering, and the check no longer freezes the app while it does (rank 5, phase 0)
key_paths: src/api/unlock.py; src/api/startup_status.py; src/monitoring/forensics.py; src/static/unlock.html; src/static/unlock.js; tests/test_unlock_recovery_progress.py; tests/test_failed_open_wal_facts.py; tests/unlock_recovery_node_test.js
summary: Unlocking an encrypted store left with a large -wal showed only an elapsed clock for as long as the passphrase check ran (24.7 s on the field's S3 boot), and sqlcipher3's close() held the GIL through the write-back so the whole process, the event loop included, stood still. While the check runs on a log above the resting ceiling (64 MiB by default, and never read below 64 MiB) the unlock page now says how big the log is, what this machine's own last measured recovery implies (named, absent when there is none, never a constant) and the seconds elapsed, through GET /api/system/unlock-progress (served while the app is locked: numbers only, inactive outside an attempt, cleared in a finally); forensics keeps last_recovery apart from last_unlock and carries it across boots and into the diagnostics block. The verify connection checkpoints through execute before it closes (measured on a 600 MiB log: close() 2.1 s with a 2.1 s worst gap; the same backfill through execute as a TRUNCATE checkpoint, worst gap 0.006 to 0.023 s; a PASSIVE one took 1.7 s with a 0.01 s worst gap), so the page can be answered meanwhile. A wrong passphrase at the right page size still pays the close-time checkpoint inside connect (measured in a Chromium walk at 1.34 s for 700 MiB, 8.95 s for 1.5 GiB and 5.84 s for 3 GiB: it follows the log's content, not its size alone); no call-site fix exists, connect.py is unchanged and four facts are pinned in tests/test_failed_open_wal_facts.py. Sentences in 12 locales. Walked in headless Chromium on seeded encrypted stores (2026-10-01): with the right passphrase the event loop was frozen 10.1 s before the fix and answered within 54 to 80 ms after it.
